questions.question: A pod in AKS has the status CrashLoopBackOff. You need to view the output of the container instance that crashed. Which command should you run?

options.why: Correct. --previous returns the logs of the last terminated container instance.
This lists nodes and does not show container output.
This applies a manifest and does not show logs.
This configures kubectl access and does not show logs.

questions.explanation: kubectl logs --previous shows the output from the container that crashed.

questions.question: A pod in AKS has the status ImagePullBackOff. Which TWO commands help you determine the cause?

options.why: Correct. The Events section shows the pull error, such as not found or unauthorized.

options.text: az aks check-acr --name aks-rag --resource-group rg-ai --acr contosoacr.azurecr.io
options.why: Correct. This verifies that the cluster can authenticate to and pull from the registry.
The container never started, so there are no application logs.
This changes the Deployment instead of diagnosing the cause.

questions.explanation: Image pull failures are recorded as events, and az aks check-acr validates registry access from the cluster.

questions.question: A container app revision fails to start. You need to view platform messages about image pulls, probe failures, and revision provisioning for the app. Which command should you run?

options.text: az containerapp logs show --name ragapi --resource-group rg-ai --type system
options.why: Correct. System logs contain platform events for the app and its revisions.

options.text: az containerapp logs show --name ragapi --resource-group rg-ai --type console
options.why: Console logs contain the container's stdout and stderr, not platform messages.
This changes the revision mode and does not show logs.
This shows ACR task build logs, not container app logs.

questions.explanation: Container Apps system logs show what the platform did, and console logs show what the app wrote.

questions.question: You need to write a Log Analytics query that returns the standard output written by a container app named ragapi. Which table should you query?

options.why: Correct. Console logs from Container Apps are stored in ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL.
This table stores platform system logs, not application output.
This table stores control-plane operations on Azure resources.
This table stores agent heartbeat records.

questions.explanation: Container Apps application output goes to ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL when the environment logs to Log Analytics.

questions.question: Pods for a Deployment in AKS are running, but their READY column shows 0/1 and the Service receives no traffic. What should you check first?

options.text: The readiness probe configuration and the Unhealthy events for the pods
options.why: Correct. A failing readiness probe keeps pods out of the Service endpoints.
The image was pulled successfully, so the registry is not the cause.

options.text: The number of nodes in the cluster
options.why: The pods are already scheduled and running.
The version does not explain a pod that is running but not ready.

questions.explanation: Pods that are running but not ready usually fail their readiness probe, which kubectl describe pod shows as Unhealthy events.
